subject.title: [Bug]: Discord elevated allowFrom fallback from channels.discord.allowFrom does not work on 2026.3.22

question: Should OpenClaw restore the shipped Discord elevated fallback from `channels.discord.allowFrom`, or keep explicit `tools.elevated.allowFrom.discord` as the required security contract?
rationale: The latest release promised the fallback, but current main docs removed that promise and restoring it changes who may reach elevated host exec from Discord.

options.title: Restore the narrow fallback
options.body: Implement a Discord-owned `allowFromFallback` hook used by both runtime and `sandbox explain`, with tests for omitted config, explicit empty override, account scope, and per-agent restriction.

options.title: Keep explicit-only elevated allowlists
options.body: Treat the current main docs as the intended security policy, document the release mismatch, and close this issue once the next release no longer promises the fallback.

options.title: Defer for broader auth redesign
options.body: Leave the issue open as a tracked security/product decision until command authorization and elevated authorization are redesigned together.

recommendation.title: Restore the narrow fallback
recommendation.body: Implement a Discord-owned `allowFromFallback` hook used by both runtime and `sandbox explain`, with tests for omitted config, explicit empty override, account scope, and per-agent restriction.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current docs correction and prior elevated/plugin boundary work that frames this security-policy choice.
